text:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: continuous-batching KV cache growth detected in serving-pool us-west-2 at 2129991234. KV cache memory > 92%, paging > 35%, tail latency spike. Auto-mitigation not triggered.

ashley.r: taking it. looking at dashboards now. can someone post recent config for continuous batching on prod pool?

mikec: pushing the config we have on the pool. continuous_batch.max_batch_tokens=524288, continuous_batch.max_num_seqs=256, continuous_batch.timeout_ms=500

mikec: snippet:
```
pool: serving-prod-usw2
continuous_batch:
  max_batch_tokens: 524288
  max_num_seqs: 256
  timeout_ms: 500
```

priya.p: that max_batch_tokens looks extreme for our token distributions. could cause enormous KV cache retention + big combined batches that blow up memory and cause paging + evictions.

jordan.l: observing a perf cliff around sequence length 12k requests — memory spikes then CPU stalls. KV eviction rate jumped x10; objects keep being pinned by long batching windows.

ashley.r: customer impact? evan_cs please advise.

evan_cs: two enterprise customers reporting increased 504s and slower streaming. One tenant sees 2x p95 latency, some timeouts for real-time agents. CS flagged urgent.

action: reduce batch size and num_seqs, shorten timeout for safety fast roll.

mikec: agree. proposing hotfix: set max_batch_tokens=32768, max_num_seqs=32, timeout_ms=200 and enable eviction_throttle=true. will do canary on 5% first.

ashley.r: do it. annotate runbook and CI. also we need to patch the default config to avoid regression.

mikec: running rollout command now:
```
redwoodctl deploy-config --pool serving-prod-usw2 \
  --set continuous_batch.max_batch_tokens=32768 \
  --set continuous_batch.max_num_seqs=32 \
  --set continuous_batch.timeout_ms=200 \
  --set runtime.eviction_throttle=true \
  --canary 5
```

sre-bot: Deploy started by mikec at 2129991250. Change id: cfg-99281. Canary target: 5% nodes.

priya.p: monitoring KV cache size and paging counters. hooking into Grafana panel 'kvcache.v2.size' and 'paging.rate'

jordan.l: tailing logs for OOMs and corruption; no new OOMs in canary nodes so far.

mikec: canary succeeded after 4m. rolling to 50%.

ashley.r: notify ops and CS. evan_cs share customer status.

evan_cs: first customer reported faster recovery, 504s dropping to near baseline. I'll post status update to their channel and offer mitigation credits if needed.

mikec: rolling to 100% now.

sre-bot: Rollout reached 100% at 2129991283. Change id: cfg-99281. No failed hosts.

priya.p: KV cache size snapshot: before rollout ~1.2TB across pool; 10m after canary ~420GB; 20m after ~310GB. paging rate normalized.

jordan.l: tail latencies p95 back to normal. no regression in throughput. looks like misconfig was root cause.

ashley.r: marking incident as mitigated. next steps: 1) formal postmortem 2) change default continuous_batch profile to conservative values 3) add alert on max_batch_tokens anomaly and a validation in config push 4) follow up with impacted customers.

evan_cs: I'll follow up with customers and log timeline.

mikec: opened PR to update default config and added config validation preventing max_batch_tokens > 100k for production pools: PR #3245.

sre-bot: Incident mitigated at 2129991290. Closing loop. :white_check_mark:

ashley.r: handing off to priya for on-call notes and postmortem lead. priya you ok to own?

priya.p: taking it. will schedule 1h postmortem and include config-change gating. will add timeline to pagerduty incident.

jordan.l: :thumbsup:

mikec: :thumbsup:
